ignoreRules.reason: Cyan-on-dark is this product's incumbent identity, not a default reached for. It is recorded as a brand commitment in PRODUCT.md and specified in DESIGN.md as The Indicator Rule: the accent is legal on exactly four things (primary action, current selection, value being edited, live state). It measures 10.15-11.73:1 against every surface in the dark theme, and the light theme replaces it with a warm-paper palette rather than inverting. Re-examine this waiver if the accent ever starts appearing on decoration.

The three flagged glows are 5-6px status lamps -- preview live, connection state, unsaved changes -- where a soft halo is the literal referent, and DESIGN.md documents the state-badge family that owns them. The one glow that WAS decoration, a 16px saturated bloom under the Solve button, was removed rather than waived.

Flagged on .result-title, which is uppercase monospace. Tracking is correct for uppercase, and the value was brought down from .07em to .03em anyway. Retained as a waiver in case the rule re-fires on the remaining uppercase micro-labels, which are the system's only heading idiom.

Verified false positive. The detector compares bounding rects without honoring scroll clipping; the jobs rail and the parameter rail are both overflow:auto (rail measured clientHeight 626 against scrollHeight 1189), so the reported elements are below the fold rather than overlapping the status rail. Confirmed in the live DOM.

One finding, on the Solve button's kbd hint, and it is a gradient-sampling artifact. The detector composites the hint's rgba(0,0,0,.16) ground against the page background because the button's background is a gradient it cannot sample, giving 1.6:1. The hint actually sits on the cyan gradient: #0a3540 over the gradient's midpoint measures 5.27:1. The light theme's version of this WAS a real failure at 3.09:1 and was fixed in tokens.css rather than waived. Re-verify this waiver by hand if the Solve button's background ever stops being a gradient.

Reports 11px body text. 11px is this system's deliberate floor, set in DESIGN.md's type scale, and the rule that matters -- undersized-ui-text, whose floor is also 11px -- passes clean at 0 findings. Density is a stated product requirement (PRODUCT.md: ~119 parameters and ~28 runs visible at once), and DESIGN.md's Density Rule requires any change that costs visible rows to justify itself. Raising the floor to 12px across the board would cost rows for no legibility gain the 11px floor does not already deliver.

All 32 are flush-by-design surfaces: viewport-tool-group and action-menu-split are segmented controls, where an inset between the segments and their shared border is exactly what the control must not have, and dv-groupview is the dock frame, which DESIGN.md specifies as carrying no internal padding of its own because its contents own their gutters.

The four remaining are dockview's own nested split containers, which must clip -- that is how a dock works. The finding that mattered, panel popovers trapped inside them, was fixed by portalling those popovers to <body> (see prefs/AnchoredPanel.tsx) rather than by loosening the dock's overflow.

The single `transition: width, height` is in dockview's vendored stylesheet (node_modules/dockview/dist/styles/dockview.css), not in this project's CSS. This project's own bare `transition: .12s` shorthands were replaced with named properties.
